newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, June 18.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, June 18.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 share index weakened for the third straight session, laid low by a cocktail of interest rate worries, a declining Dow, weak futures and nerves ahead of the new government's July 2 Budget. The leading share index closed 25.2 points lower at 4,657. It has dropped 125 points this week since reaching a record closing high on Friday.

FRANKFURT - Electronic trade in German shares ended with the IBIS DAX index in positive territory, matching the bourse closing level from earlier on in trade mostly driven by derivatives. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,730.27, down 11.21 points, or 0.30 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,730.56, up 9.38 points, or 0.25 percent.

PARIS - Shares closed weaker after a day of relatively light trading amid investor caution ahead of Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's debut parliamentary policy speech on Thursday. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,751.74, down 10.86 points, or 0.39 percent.

ZURICH - Massive gains in Novartis stock led Swiss shares one percent higher to record levels, with the Swiss Market Index (SMI) ending above 5,400 points for the first time. The Swiss market index closed at 5,405.0, up 59.1 points, or 1.11 percent.

MILAN - Stock prices surged, ending at session highs, in the wake of soaring Btp bond futures betting all on European convergence and a narrowing of the spread over German bunds. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 12,930, up 213 points, or 1.67 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Shares closed mostly lower with only a 6.9 percent rise in Philips pushing the AEX share index into positive territory. The AEX index closed at 849.13, up 1.98 points, or 0.23 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed down, but losses were limited as the dollar/yen rate did not react much to the big rise in Japan's trade surplus for May, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,497.85, down 95.81 points, or 0.47 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended easier but trimmed afternoon losses following a bout of late buying on utilities that lifted the Hang Seng Index up from its day's low of 13,999.69, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,203.89, down 103.26 points, or 0.72 percent.

SYDNEY - Stocks meandered to an easier close, with the only highlight being a late annnouncement confirming the merger of the nickel operations of QNI Ltd and South Africa's Gencor Ltd. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,673.4, down 8.3 points, or 0.31 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended mixed, but an enormous asset swap deal by broker SBC Warburg boosted turnover into record territory, dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said. The All-share index closed at 7,218.4, up 26.3 points, or 0.37 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,096.7, down 3.8 points, or 0.01 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,432.1, down 0.6 points, or 0.35 percent.
